### 1 — Scene
Sliced roast beef with a leafy quinoa salad, cooked leafy greens, and a little onion and dark-red garnish.

### 2 — Vessel
A large, rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a circular approximation: **3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

### 3–6 — Items, area, volume, and weight
Area shares below total **90%**, consistent with a mostly covered plate. Dressing is counted separately as a coating, not additional plate coverage.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sliced roast beef | 29% | 154 × 1.4 = 216 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 205 g |
| Mixed salad leaves | 33% | 175 × 2.8 = 490 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 74 g |
| Cooked quinoa scattered through salad | 10% | 53 × 0.9 = 48 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 38 g |
| Cooked leafy greens and red stems, likely chard | 13% | 69 × 1.5 = 104 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 62 g |
| Cooked onion strips | 3% | 16 × 0.9 = 14 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 9 g |
| Dark-red garnish, likely dried tomato | 2% | 11 × 0.7 = 8 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 5 g |
| Oil/dressing coating | — | Approximately 7 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 7 g |

### 7 — Energy
Using cooked/as-plated values: beef **250**, salad leaves **20**, quinoa **120**, cooked chard **35**, onions **45**, dried tomato **200**, and oil **880 kcal/100 g**.

Estimated contributions are **513 + 15 + 46 + 22 + 4 + 10 + 62 = 672 kcal**.

### 8 — Sanity check
**Approximately 400 g and 670 kcal** is plausible for the visible plate. Most energy comes from the beef and oil; the large leafy portions contribute relatively little weight. Beef thickness and dressing quantity are the main uncertainties.
